notes: The sketch works with the on-board LED (pin 13), so the external LED circuit is optional. I built that optional circuit as the manual and images show it.
Breadboard holes are read from the image. The image labels the rows f–j along the top half, but the catalogue names the bottom bank (rows f–j) '<col>b'. So the LED, resistor and wires use bank 'b'.

The orange wire runs from pin 13 to column 3, row g. The resistor spans column 3 to column 6 on row h. The LED anode (long, bent leg) is in column 6 and the cathode is in column 8. The black wire runs from column 8, row g to the Arduino GND next to pin 13 (GND.1).
Which GND header pin is GND.1 is an assumption. The image shows the black wire at the GND pin beside pin 13.
The jumper wires have two ends, a and b. Which end goes where is arbitrary.
Breadboard hole names follow the catalogue: bank 't' is rows a-e and bank 'b' is rows f-j. In the image the a-e half is drawn at the bottom, and the button straddles the centre gap.

The button sits in columns 4 and 6. Side 1 (4b.f and 4t.e) is the 5V side, via the orange wire and the rail. Side 2 (6b.f and 6t.e) is the pin 2 and pull-down side. Which physical leg is 'l' or 'r' is an assumption.

Power rail hole numbers (bp.1, bp.3, bn.1, bn.7) are estimated from the image, counting holes from the left end of each rail. The orange wire goes to the lower (+) rail. The short black wire and the black wire from the Arduino go to the upper (-) rail of the bottom pair, which I named 'bn'.
The red wire goes to the Uno 5V pin. The black wire goes to the second GND pin on the power header, named GND.2.
The 10K resistor spans columns 6 to 9 in row c. It is in the same strip as the button's pin 2 side and the teal signal wire. The black wire from 9t.b takes its other end to ground.
The tutorial's sketch (built-in LED on pin 13) needs no extra wiring.

The manual only says to wire each button to a different GPIO pin and refers to a video and a generic wiring snippet. I used the GPIO numbers from the full code listing (4, 17, 27, 10), with each button's other side going to GND.
Parts count follows the manual: 5 pin-to-socket jumpers (4 GPIO + 1 GND) and 4 pin-to-pin jumpers (one ground link per button).

The exact breadboard columns and rows are assumed. Each button straddles the centre gap, with side 1 (1.l/1.r) in the top half and side 2 (2.l/2.r) in the bottom half. The GPIO lead goes into the top strip of side 1, and the pin-to-pin lead goes from the bottom strip of side 2 to the bottom negative rail.
For the pin-to-socket jumpers, port a is the male pin end (breadboard) and port b is the female socket end (Pi header pin).
The Raspberry Pi is a new part type that lists only the header pins this circuit uses. All GND pins are treated as one node.
The speakers or headphones plug into the Pi's audio jack, not the GPIO header. They are not modelled because the manual gives no wiring for them and the audio jack is not a catalogue port.
The pygame and gpiozero code, the sound samples and Thonny are software and are not part of the graph.
